Messages.Body:
8/2/99 Editors Corner - Ethan Burrow, Prince of Austin

I just sent off my application for Crusade : Austin, it's going to be
held October 30, 1999. Please spread the word.

I'd like to take this moment to say how much 10 hour work days suck, yet
I still somehow managed to get this newsletter out - albeit shorter than
normal. Hopefully we'll have some juicy info to pore over next month
after Gen-Con.

Vampire of the Month -

Lolita

Aside from being a good filler for Ventrue decks, she's also the
cheapest capacity vampire in the clan with Presence. She's really only
useful if your crypt is already too expensive, and you need to bring the
average capacity down. Do NOT put her into a combat deck unless you
somehow decided to experiment with Fortitude and Toreador Antitribu.

Card of the Month -

Alacrity

The only +1 stealth action modifier card available to our clan. The
superior really isn't all that useful, since you pretty much want the
action to succeed if you're willing to pay 2 blood. It's really
expensive, but sometimes the surprise stealth will give you a big
advantage if your opponents are playing with light intercept. Otherwise
you're better off expecting to get blocked.

Playing inferior celerity on Jost may allow you to increase his
stealth/bleed potential. See the March issue regarding Jost and
Stealth/Bleed.

How the Recent Rules Team Rulings affect the Toreador Antitribu

Since the Toreador-Antitribu are among the few clans that can pull off
voting decks, noting the new effects of banishment is important. You can
re-influence your "created" vamps, and the owner of the vamp, not the
controller, gets it during uncontrolled. Our playgroups exposure to the
Mind Rape/Banishment deck brought about this ruling, and I applaud it.

Soul Burn now affects the current strike as well as future strikes. So
we're no longer as safe at range from the Tremere with our weapons.
Expect them to start playing with more Soul Burns to stave off our guns.

The life boon ruling is very annoying, so make sure to pack sudden
reversals in tournament play if it's prevelent in your area.

Deck Medic/Strategy Corner

See the August Tzimisce Newsletter for the Vicissitude/Obfuscate deck I
mentioned in the last newsletter.

There has also been a lot of talk on the newsgroup regarding Toreador's
ability to compete as a Clan. If you have any strategy or decks refuting
this assertion (at least for the Toreador Antitribu) please forward them
to me for inclusion in the next newsletter.

Messages.Body:
Ethan Burrow wrote:
> How the Recent Rules Team Rulings affect the Toreador Antitribu
>
> Since the Toreador-Antitribu are among the few clans that can pull off
> voting decks, noting the new effects of banishment is important. You can
> re-influence your "created" vamps, and the owner of the vamp, not the
> controller, gets it during uncontrolled. Our playgroups exposure to the
> Mind Rape/Banishment deck brought about this ruling, and I applaud it.

A slight correction/clarification:

If the Banished vamp is under a *transient* change-of-control effect
(Malk Dementia, Mind Rape, etc.) from a card no longer in play, then he
is placed in his "previous controller"'s uncontrolled region, not
necessarily the "owner"'s uncontrolled region. The question is one of
underlying control, not of ownership. And the question doesn't come up
for vampires who have been permanently stolen (via Corruption or
Hostile Takeover, for example), since there is no "underlying control".
